1041-performance-2: 12 credits of large ensembles by audition, 4 of small, and 6 from the list. MUEN courses can repeat.
1043-performance-2: 10 credits from the list. MUEN courses can repeat.
1044-program-description: Full jazz training: theory, harmony, keyboard, history, practice, improvisation, composition and arranging, with lessons, orchestras, ensembles and combos.
1044-special-requirements: B- minimum in all Jazz courses, lessons, exams, combos and ensembles. At most two consecutive years with the same teacher.
1044-prerequisite-courses: 22 credits. Auditions, placement tests or equivalents can exempt you. Guitarists and pianists skip MUJZ 170 and 171.
1045-large-ensemble: 8–12 credits. Rhythm section players (piano, guitar, bass, drums, vibraphone) can swap 4 for free electives. MUEN courses can repeat.
1045-elective-courses-21-25-credits: 3 of non-Music and 18–22 of free electives, without MUEN. Rhythm section players may take up to 22.
1045-program-description: Practical and theoretical training, with lessons and suitable ensembles.
1047-program-description: Orchestral or choral streams, on technique and rehearsal. Enter by audition and entrance exam; limited, not for U0.
1048-program-description: For B.Mus. students: early music practice, playing a period instrument or singing.
1049-program-description: For non-Jazz B.Mus. students, mainly classical students who love jazz and have the basics: jazz materials and tunes, analysis, writing for small and large ensembles, and history.
1049-program-description-2: Instrumental and vocal jazz, through theory and practice.
1049-special-requirements: A- minimum in lessons, exams and ensembles. Take L.Mus. Performance 1 at the end of first year, and 2 and 3 in the next two, to finish on time.
1050-ensemble-requirements: Violin, viola and cello start with four terms of string quartets. Violinists also play two terms on viola.
1051-complementary-performance-18-credit: Large ensemble and assigned small ensemble every term, part-time or full-time. 12 and 6 credits from two lists.
1052-program-description: 100 credits, with options in various instruments.
1052-complementary-performance-18-credit: Large ensemble every term. 12 from the list; MUEN 570 for four terms; 2 more of MUEN 570 or 574.
1053-complementary-performance-21-credit: Large ensemble every term. 12 and 9 from two lists; 400–500 level MUEN up to 4.
1055-practical-instruction-muin-courses: Private lessons, with extra fees and term limits by program (p. 1010): required in your major, as a jazz or early music minor, or as electives on a second instrument with approval.

You can't take only lessons in a term; take your other required courses too. Submit the Request Form by the deadline each year, for lessons or voice coaching; the Faculty adds MUIN courses once you have a registered course.
1055-examinations-and-goals-in-practical: Levels depend on your program, repertoire difficulty and how well you play. Five categories: Concentration, Major, Licentiate, Postgraduate and Elective Study.
1055-concentration-study: Music Studies, Composition, Education, History and Theory present one Concentration Final Exam (MUIN 283). C or higher in all practical work.
1055-examination: Shows you qualify for the B.Mus. If not ready, the panel may recommend withdrawal or a retry. At least two staff apart from your teacher, one from the area, appointed by the Performance Chair; your teacher may join panels of three or more. The mark is the panel's average.
1055-major-study: You must show talent to be admitted. Exams and recitals are set by the program.
1056-examinations: Three stages, each with at least three staff appointed by the Chair, one possibly your teacher, and an averaged mark.

First exam: checks progress and whether you continue or are asked to withdraw. Second: performing a program of suitable length and repertoire. Recitals: public, before a jury, showing technical mastery and style.
1056-licentiate-study: You must show talent to be admitted. A- or higher in all practical work.
1056-examinations-2: Three stages, each with at least three staff appointed by the Chair, one possibly your teacher, and an averaged mark.

L.Mus. Performance 1: checks progress and whether you continue or are asked to withdraw. Then a public recital showing solo competence, with accompaniment for non-keyboard players and singers. Final recital: technical mastery and style, before a jury.
1057-postgraduate-study: M.Mus., Artist Diploma, Graduate Diploma and D.Mus.: see graduate requirements.
1057-elective-practical-instruction-elec: An extra year on your main instrument or voice, or lessons on a second, as MUIN electives. Extra fees may apply (p. 1010). See the Elective Lessons site.
1057-registration-withdrawal: Not in Minerva. Submit the Online Request Form by the deadline. To withdraw, email teacherpreference.music@mcgill.ca; see p. 1014.
1057-assignment-of-teachers: The Performance Chair assigns teachers, considering requests. Returning students keep theirs unless arranged. Late forms cost $50 with no guarantee. Assignments are confirmed in week one; you then arrange lesson times.
Lessons missed by your teacher get made up; yours only with 48 hours' notice. Degree and diploma lessons must be with Schulich staff.
1057-practical-examinations: Concentration or performance exams with an MUIN code, not in Minerva; apply by form. Requirements by area: Brass, Early Music, Guitar, Harp, Jazz, Organ, Percussion, Piano, Strings, Voice, Woodwinds.
1058-application-for-practical-examinati: In official exam periods. Final-year students may request early September (MUIN 283, 482, 452); September 2027 counts as Summer 2027. You pick material with your teacher and apply online.

Application / withdrawal: Fall, October 15 / November 15, 2026. Winter, February 15 / March 15, 2027. Later withdrawal is normally for illness; otherwise the Chair must authorize it. Deferrals go to the next December or April. Late applications need the Chair's permission and $50.
1058-special-procedures-for-september-ex: For Summer graduands only, with no supplementals, not in Minerva. September 2–4, 2026: application or withdrawal by May 31; recital program by August 1, 2026. Late: Chair's permission and $50.
1058-examination-marking: The average of all examiners. Pass: L.Mus. A-; B.Mus. Performance B-; other B.Mus. C. In MUIN 452 and 482, if the average passes but most fail you, you get the grade just below.
1059-nursing-ingram-school-of: Prepares nurses for public and global health with high standards, research and collaboration. Uses Strengths-Based Nursing, developed by McGill's Dr. Laurie Gottlieb, RN, in new facilities with modern learning labs.
1059-mission: Educate nurses, advance nursing, and improve health and health equity globally.
1059-vision: Conditions for health and healing through knowledgeable, compassionate, strengths-based nursing.
